title: Exceptional inverse image of a smooth morphism commutes with extension of coefficients
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ has characteristic $p>0$, $\ell\ne p$ is prime, and $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix its coefficient-independent compactification. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings, each annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Write $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ for complexes of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $R_T$ with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Use derived coefficient extension $K_B=K\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], the constructible adjunctions $Rf_{!,R}\dashv f_R^!$ for $R=A,B$ [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], and the canonical compact-support comparison $b$ [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. For a common annihilator $N=\ell^n$ of $A,B$, the Tate line is the inverse image from the etale site of $\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$; write $K(d)=K\otimes^L_R R_T(1)^{\otimes d}$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist].

For
$K\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ let

$$
c_{A,B}(K):(f_A^!K)_B\longrightarrow f_B^!(K_B)\quad\text{in }\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)
$$

be the unique morphism (the transpose under $Rf_{!,B}\dashv f_B^!$) satisfying

$$
\varepsilon_B(K_B)\circ Rf_{!,B}\bigl(c_{A,B}(K)\bigr)
=(\varepsilon_A(K))_B\circ b(f_A^!K)^{-1}.
$$

Then $c_{A,B}(K)$ is natural in $K$ and is an isomorphism. On a coordinate
chart $f|_U=p_d\circ e$ (with $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ étale and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is the chart inclusion, where
$j^*f_A^!\simeq e^*p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$ is the counit-preserving identification for the chart adjunction whose counit is summation over the fibres of $e$ followed by the affine-space counit of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], transported from the etale site) it is the canonical isomorphism
$(e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d])_B\simeq e^*p_d^*(K_B)(d)[2d]$.

proof.text: Put $F_R=Rf_{!,R}$, $G_R=f_R^!$ and $T=(-)_B$. The three cited statements type $T\epsilon_A\,b(G_A-)^{-1}$. Its adjunction transpose defines $c$ uniquely, with the required identity. Naturality of $b,\epsilon_A$ and the adjunction Hom bijection proves naturality of $c$.

Choose the finite admissible cover $fj_a=p_de_a$ of [lem-sp-smooth-admissible-coordinate-cover]. In particular each $e_a$ is separated etale of finite type over the original base, and every scheme and open inclusion meets the chart adjunction hypotheses.

source.place: Charts: admissible coordinate cover; retained Step 13

proof.text: The splitting/trace equation [lem-sp-p1-splitting-scalar] and actual P1 counit [lem-sp-p1-counit-scalar] feed the ordered iteration [lem-sp-affine-counit-scalar]; [lem-sp-etale-sum-counit-scalar] supplies sum evaluation. For each chart, [lem-sp-chart-left-scalar-normalization] supplies $\lambda_R:F_{d,R}De_{\Sigma!,R}\simeq F_{g,R}$, preserving the composite counit, and identifies the pasted scalar map with the specified $\beta_g$, including refinement to the fixed compactification.

source.place: Charts: fixed left comparison; retained Step 11

proof.text: The scalar, pullback, Tate and shift domains agree by [lem-sp-etale-ctf-chart-domain]. By [lem-sp-chart-finite-ring-adjunction] the ordinary chart adjunction restricts to finite-Tor complexes and transfers with its actual counit. Its unique counit-preserving comparison is $\theta_R:H_{g,R}\simeq g_R^!$, where $H_{g,R}=e^*p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$.

source.place: Charts: domains and transport; retained Steps 3--4 and 11

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-chart-counit-scalar-transport]. Its pro-etale equation says that the canonical tensor map $a_g:TH_{g,A}\simeq H_{g,B}T$ has inverse transpose $T\widetilde\epsilon_{g,A}\,b_g(H_{g,A}-)^{-1}$. Transport through $\theta_A,\theta_B$ and use uniqueness of the transpose: $c_g$ is $a_g$ under these counit-preserving chart identifications.

source.place: Charts: normalized coefficient counit; retained Steps 5--11

proof.text: The exact pro-etale open adjunction has the scalar counit identity of [lem-sp-open-proetale-counit-scalar], with right mate the canonical restriction/tensor map $a_j$. For $(j,f)$ the cancellation theorem [lem-sp-open-exceptional-scalar-locality] therefore gives $c_{fj}=j^*(c_f)a_j(G_{f,A}-)$. Thus each $j_a^*c_f$ is the chart map $a_g$ from Step 5, an isomorphism. The open-cover detection clause (3) of [det-sf-mate-open-restriction] now proves $c_f$ invertible. The same equality proves the stated canonical chart formula.

source.place: Locality: source-open comparison and detection; retained Steps 12--13
